key_insight: Subtle, purposeful bugs can make ML research appear valid while changing conclusions; ASMR-Bench provides a concrete benchmark to evaluate whether auditors can detect such sabotage in research codebases.
problem_solved: Addresses the risk that misaligned or malicious AI/agents (or humans) can introduce hard-to-detect sabotage into ML experiments, producing misleading results that evade standard checks and peer review.
method: Curate 9 real ML research codebases and produce carefully crafted sabotaged variants that change qualitative experimental outcomes while remaining plausible.
Define tasks and evaluation protocols that measure an auditor's ability to detect, localize, and explain sabotaging changes across variants.
Provide metrics and controlled scenarios to benchmark auditing tools, human reviewers, and automated defenses against sabotage.
impact: Provides a standardized way to test and improve auditing practices, tooling, and policies to protect research integrity and reduce risk from misaligned or adversarial agents in ML research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: clean codebase → sabotage injection → experimental outputs → auditor analysis/decision
Side-by-side result comparison (plots or table) illustrating original vs. sabotaged experimental outcomes
Heatmap/confusion matrix of auditor detection performance across the 9 codebases and sabotage types
Annotated code diff highlighting a subtle sabotaging change (e.g., off-by-one, optimizer tweak) with explanation bubbles
paper_title: ASMR-Bench: Auditing for Sabotage in ML Research
paper_authors: Eric Gan, Aryan Bhatt, Buck Shlegeris, Julian Stastny, Vivek Hebbar
